mnemonic: A matter 事 with a reason 故 sat behind it that nobody in the world wanted. He came out of it hurt: じこ.
notes: 出来事 できごと is any occurrence at all. 事故 is specifically an accident, and 発生 はっせい is the word that goes with it.
sentence: 彼は事故で怪我をしました。
sentence_meaning: He was injured in an accident.

mnemonic: A garment 衣 standing in 代 for a container, which is what a bag amounts to. No, thank you: ふくろ.
sentence: 袋はいりません。
sentence_meaning: I don't need a bag.

mnemonic: A hand 手 branching off 派 louder than everybody else's. She went down on the ice in front of the entire street: はで.
notes: 地味 じみ is the opposite, plain and quiet. 派手 is not always an insult.
sentence: 雪道で派手に転んでしまったの。
sentence_meaning: I slipped spectacularly at the snowy road.

meaning: now (when it's too late), at this stage
mnemonic: Now 今 of all moments, and again 更 after all of this. Regretting it at this stage is no use to anybody: いまさら.
sentence: 今更後悔しても、もう遅いよ。
sentence_meaning: It is too late for regrets now.

mnemonic: True 真 straight 直, both characters saying it and neither of them bending. Down this road and keep going: まっすぐ.
notes: 素直 すなお is straightforward about a person, honest and unresisting. 真っ直ぐ is a line, and it does an honest person as well.
sentence: この道を真っ直ぐ行ってください。
sentence_meaning: Please go straight along this road.

mnemonic: The oil 油 runs out 断 and the machine seizes, which is what dropping your guard for one second does. It ends in a big accident: ゆだん.
notes: 油断大敵 is the set phrase: carelessness is the great enemy.
sentence: 少しの油断が大きな事故につながります。
sentence_meaning: A little carelessness can cause a big accident.

mnemonic: You put the car into the wall rather than the wall coming over to meet you. Mine, this morning: ぶつける.
notes: ぶつかる is a thing hitting something. ぶつける is you hitting something with it.
sentence: 車を壁にぶつけてしまいました。
sentence_meaning: I hit my car into the wall.

meaning: to be brought up, to grow
mnemonic: Nobody is doing it to them, they are getting on with it themselves. The vegetables are coming along nicely: そだつ.
notes: 育てる そだてる is somebody raising them. 育つ is them growing.
sentence: 野菜がよく育っている。
sentence_meaning: The vegetables are growing well.

mnemonic: The mark 傷 lands and stays, and this one was made out of words rather than anything you could point at: きずつく.
notes: 傷つける きずつける is hurting somebody. 傷つく is being hurt, and it covers feelings as readily as skin.
sentence: 私は彼女の言葉に傷つきました。
sentence_meaning: Her words hurt me.

mnemonic: Something gets let go 発 and travels out from you. Not one word of it, all evening: はっする.
sentence: 彼は一言も発することはなかった。
sentence_meaning: He did not utter a single word.

mnemonic: Ended 終 and finished 了, both halves of it, which is how you announce a thing rather than how you say it. Five past seven: しゅうりょう.
notes: 終わり おわり is the end as a noun in speech. 終了 is the formal one, on signs and announcements.
sentence: コンサートは夜7時5分に終了しました。
sentence_meaning: The concert ended at 7:05 pm.

mnemonic: The sound 音 that a foot 足 makes, and there is a great deal of it coming down the corridor: あしおと.
sentence: 廊下から大きな足音が聞こえた。
sentence_meaning: I could hear loud footsteps from the hallway.

mnemonic: The channel is cut 決 and the mind 意 only runs one way now. His is not about to shift: けつい.
notes: 判断 はんだん is a judgement you make about something and 覚悟 かくご is being ready for what follows. 決意 is the deciding itself.
sentence: 彼の決意は堅いな。
sentence_meaning: His decision is firm.

mnemonic: Your heart 心 feels 感 something about what somebody else managed to do. He stuck it out and you noticed: かんしん.
notes: 関心 かんしん written with 関 is a different word entirely, interest rather than admiration, and it sounds identical.
sentence: 彼の我慢強さには感心しました。
sentence_meaning: I admired his perseverance.

mnemonic: It goes down 飲 and in 込 in one movement, and the same verb does taking an idea in whole. The entire dose: のみこむ.
sentence: 彼は薬を一気に飲み込んだ。
sentence_meaning: He swallowed all of the medicine in one go.

mnemonic: Turn the thing over 反 and stand it up as though it were so, which is not the same as it being so. Even if it were true: かりに.
notes: もし is if. 仮に is supposing for the sake of argument, and it is the more formal of the two.
sentence: 仮にそれが事実だとしても、もう遅いよ。
sentence_meaning: Even if that were true, it's too late now anyway.

mnemonic: Grass 艹 and fruit 果 worked into something that is not a meal and was never meant to be. Round to everybody: おかし.
notes: 甘い あまい is sweet as a taste. お菓子 is sweets as the things you eat.
sentence: みんなにお菓子をあげましょう。
sentence_meaning: Let's give everyone some sweets.

meaning: to be dyed, to be tainted
mnemonic: Water and a tree between them, and the colour goes the whole way through rather than sitting on the surface. Hemp takes it well: そまる.
notes: 染める そめる is you dyeing something. 染まる is it taking the colour, and both of them do being tainted by the company you keep.
sentence: 麻はきれいに染まります。
sentence_meaning: Hemp dyes nicely.

mnemonic: The bamboo bending 笑 and the sound that comes with it, and in that house it does not let up: わらい.
sentence: あの家は笑いが絶えないね。
sentence_meaning: Laughter never stops in that house.

mnemonic: Buying 買 things 物, which is precisely what the word says and not a syllable more. At the supermarket: かいもの.
sentence: スーパーで買い物をします。
sentence_meaning: I will go shopping at the supermarket.

mnemonic: An open mouth and the same sound coming out of it twice over. I had never heard that one: うた.
notes: 歌う うたう is the verb. 歌 is the song itself.
sentence: 私はその歌を知らなかった。
sentence_meaning: I didn't know that song.

mnemonic: The shelter 广 is the house, and this is the ground beside it with nothing built on top. There is a dog on it: にわ.
sentence: 庭に犬がいます。
sentence_meaning: There is a dog in the yard.

mnemonic: A thing 物 that happens to be alive 生, which covers a good deal more than the ones with faces. Look after them: いきもの.
sentence: 生き物を大切にしましょう。
sentence_meaning: Let's care about living things.

mnemonic: Set apart 特 and then set apart again 殊, which is more than merely unusual. He can do something nobody else can: とくしゅ.
notes: 特別 とくべつ is special as in singled out for treatment. 特殊 is special as in of a different kind altogether.
sentence: 彼は特殊な能力を持っています。
sentence_meaning: He has a special ability.

mnemonic: You take somebody along 連 and go 行 with them, away from where you are standing now. Take me as well: つれていく.
notes: 連れて来る つれてくる is the same trip in the other direction, bringing them back here, and 連れる つれる is the plain verb behind both.
sentence: 私も連れて行ってください。
sentence_meaning: Please take me along.

mnemonic: The state 状 of the thing as it actually is 現 rather than as anybody would prefer. We cannot fix it, and that is where we are: げんじょう.
sentence: 問題を解決できないのが現状です。
sentence_meaning: The current situation is that we can't solve the problem.

mnemonic: A big 大 part 分 of the way there, said about progress rather than about size. Your piano has come on: だいぶ.
notes: Read おおいた the same characters are the prefecture. とても is very as a plain intensifier, where 大分 is considerably, about how far along a thing has got.
sentence: 大分ピアノが上手くなりました。
sentence_meaning: You've gotten pretty good at the piano.

mnemonic: The base 氐 underneath the shelter 广, which is the lowest part there is of a thing. The cup has a wet one: そこ.
notes: Same reading as そこ, there, which is written in kana. 底 is the bottom of something.
sentence: コップの底が濡れていますよ。
sentence_meaning: The bottom of the cup is wet.

mnemonic: Learning 学 as your life 生 for a few years, which is what the two characters actually say. My brother is one: がくせい.
notes: 生徒 せいと is a pupil at school. 学生 is properly a university student, though it gets used more loosely than that.
sentence: 弟は学生です。
sentence_meaning: My younger brother is a student.

mnemonic: Nailed down 丁 and settled 寧, which about work means nothing skipped and about speech means nothing rough. She always is: ていねい.
sentence: 彼女はいつも丁寧に仕事をします。
sentence_meaning: She always works carefully.

mnemonic: The frame 範 drawn round 囲 the thing, and whatever is inside it counts. As far as you happen to know: はんい.
sentence: 知っている範囲で教えてください。
sentence_meaning: Please tell us as much as you know.

mnemonic: Straight out of English and then cut in half, television down to テレビ, which is what Japanese does to long loanwords: テレビ.
notes: The shortening is everywhere once you see it: パソコン, コンビニ, スマホ.
sentence: 家にテレビはありません。
sentence_meaning: I don't have a television at home.

mnemonic: A beautiful 美 person 人, and in practice the word is used of women. His mother is one: びじん.
notes: Said of women almost exclusively. 綺麗 きれい does the job as an adjective for anybody.
sentence: 彼のお母さんは美人です。
sentence_meaning: His mother's a beautiful woman.

mnemonic: What the hand 扌 has learned to do without being shown twice. His judo one is the best in the country: わざ.
notes: 技術 ぎじゅつ is technology, or technique in general, and 腕 うで is the arm and also does skill, the way English says a good hand. 技 わざ is one particular move.
sentence: 彼の柔道の技は日本一です。
sentence_meaning: His judo technique is the best in Japan.

mnemonic: What is about to 将 come 来, close enough that you can make plans about it. A pilot, if it works out: しょうらい.
notes: 未来 みらい is the future in the large sense. 将来 is your own, and near enough to plan for.
sentence: 将来はパイロットになりたいです。
sentence_meaning: I want to become a pilot in the future.

mnemonic: Written down 記 and scratched into metal 録 so that it outlasts everybody. A world one, in the marathon: きろく.
sentence: マラソンで世界記録が出た。
sentence_meaning: There was a new world record in the marathon.

mnemonic: Behaving the way an adult 大人 does, which said of a grown woman means she does not make a fuss. Mine is like that: おとなしい.
notes: Not childish and not shy either. It is the word for somebody calm and undemanding, and it is meant as a compliment. 静か しずか is quiet as in no noise.
sentence: 私の彼女はとても大人しいです。
sentence_meaning: My girlfriend's very quiet.

mnemonic: The hard part that is left when everything else has gone, and calcium is meant to be good for them: ほね.
sentence: カルシウムは骨にいいそうです。
sentence_meaning: I hear calcium is good for the bones.

mnemonic: The eye 目 fixed on the marker post 標 at the far end of the field. Hers is a clear one: もくひょう.
notes: 目的 もくてき is the purpose, why you are doing it at all. 目標 is the target you are aiming at.
sentence: 彼女には明確な目標があるね。
sentence_meaning: She has a clear goal.

mnemonic: Meat 肉 and body 体, which is the body as a physical object rather than as you. It does not last forever: にくたい.
notes: 精神 せいしん is the mind, and 肉体 is the thing it gets set against. 身体 しんたい is the body as a whole, health included, where 肉体 is the flesh of it.
sentence: 肉体はいつか滅びます。
sentence_meaning: Our bodies will perish some day.

mnemonic: You make the thing arrive at somebody's door rather than standing back and watching it get there. This, to him: とどける.
notes: 届く とどく is a thing arriving. 届ける is you delivering it.
sentence: これを彼に届けてください。
sentence_meaning: Please deliver this to him.

mnemonic: Where the foot 足 starts 元, which is exactly the part you cannot see in the dark. Watch it: あしもと.
sentence: 暗いので足元に気を付けてください。
sentence_meaning: Please watch your step in the dark.

meaning: to look for, to search for (e.g. a lost item)
mnemonic: The hand goes through the whole place after something that has gone missing, and the police are doing it to that man: さがす.
notes: Same reading as 探す さがす. 捜 is for what has gone missing, a person or a lost wallet, and 探 is for something you want and are seeking out.
sentence: 警察がその男を捜しているの。
sentence_meaning: The police are searching for that man.

mnemonic: It looked deliberate, and everybody in the ground thought so at the same moment. Not a slip: わざと.
notes: わざわざ is going out of your way to do something helpful. わざと is doing it on purpose, and often something you should not.
sentence: 彼はわざと負けたように見えたな。
sentence_meaning: It looked like he lost on purpose.

mnemonic: Offered rather than asked, with the bottle already tilted over your glass. Some wine: いかが.
notes: The polite どう. どうですか becomes いかがですか when you are being careful.
sentence: ワインはいかがですか。
sentence_meaning: Would you like some wine?

mnemonic: A hand over the thing hanging on the line, and this piece is going to end up as curtains: ぬの.
sentence: この布はカーテンに使えます。
sentence_meaning: This cloth can be used for curtains.

mnemonic: Seeds 種 sorted into groups by what they resemble 類. Roses come in a great many of them: しゅるい.
sentence: バラには色々な種類があります。
sentence_meaning: There are many varieties of rose.

mnemonic: You fill 満 the thing right the way up, and a set of requirements gets filled in exactly the same way. He does not: みたす.
notes: 満ちる みちる is a thing filling up on its own. 満たす is you filling it, or meeting a condition.
sentence: 彼は応募の条件を満たしていない。
sentence_meaning: He doesn't meet the application requirements.

mnemonic: The scene 景 and the colour 色 in it, taken together as the one thing. From up here it is worth the walk: けしき.
notes: The reading is irregular, 景 read け and 色 read しき, so learn it whole.
sentence: ここから見る景色は本当に綺麗ですね。
sentence_meaning: The scenery you see from here is really beautiful.

mnemonic: The spirit 気 for a thing you have to go and find 勇 rather than one you were born holding. He has it: ゆうき.
sentence: 彼は勇気があるね。
sentence_meaning: He has courage.
